teaser.text: Marvell Technology designs specialized chips and some optical modules that help data centers compute, connect, store, and protect information. Its business is a chain of engineering, outsourced manufacturing, and repeat customer orders, so a dollar enters through sales and leaves through factories, people, and advance commitments.

stock.title: Marvell stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Marvell's forecast weighs bear, base and bull cases, then tests cash generation and valuation against earnings and free cash flow.
stock.opening: Marvell's weighted scenario is $502.06 in October 2027 and $617.50 in October 2029, with 50% probability. It hinges on custom, optical and switching programs reaching production and producing durable margins and cash per share.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Marvell's business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: The forecast’s weighted price rises from $502.06 in October 2027 to $617.50 in October 2029. That means an 89% total return with dividends in 2027 and 133% in 2029, against today’s $265.86.

The range is wide because execution determines both earnings and the valuation investors will pay. By October 2029, the bear case gives $244.32, while the bull case gives $1,026.09. The probabilities are 30% bear, 50% base and 20% bull.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Marvell, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: EBIT is the main driver. The base EBIT is $31,500M, built from the midpoint of management’s revenue and margin targets, with ongoing stock compensation and amortization removed. Bear EBIT is $14,950M; bull EBIT is $36,400M. The range reflects a record that includes several operating losses before FY2026’s $1,322.9M reported profit, alongside a $2,891.0M adjusted result. The base requires custom, optical and switching programs to reach production; the bear assumes delayed ramps, while the bull assumes the top of management’s plan.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Marvell really make?

paragraphs.text: “Real free cash flow” subtracts stock compensation as an economic cost and was $801.1 million, or 9.8% of revenue. In Q2 FY2027, Marvell sold $111.1 million of receivables through non-recourse factoring. Factoring brings cash forward; it does not create extra sales. Cash strength therefore leads to the balance sheet and the promises against it.

blocks.heading: How much does Marvell pay per share?

paragraphs.text: The base and bull cases use $0.24 annual dividends in every window. The bear keeps $0.24 through October 2027, then cuts it to $0.12. The latest declared quarterly dividend is $0.06, and the five-year record stayed at $0.24 annually. The forecast therefore treats a freeze as most likely, with a cut only if cash generation deteriorates.

blocks.heading: Does Marvell's cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow was $1,391.9 million, almost unchanged from $1,389.6 million. Its margin fell to 17.0% from 24.1% because sales grew faster than cash conversion. Marvell also expected about $1 billion of capacity prepayments in FY2027. These payments support future production but consume cash before chips are sold.

Buybacks became the largest shareholder return. In 2026, dividends and repurchases totalled $2,245.2 million, or 161.3% of free cash flow. Asset sales supplied $2,506.0 million, so part of the payout came from converting businesses into cash rather than from that year’s operations. Buybacks can increase each remaining owner’s share of future cash, but employee compensation and acquisitions can issue shares again.

paragraphs.text: The view moves toward the bear case in FY2027–FY2028 if custom design wins fail to become high-volume shipments, customer concentration worsens or supplier prepayments rise without matching receipts. Gross-margin pressure and weaker cash conversion through FY2029 would reinforce that shift.

blocks.heading: What has Marvell guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: At its October 6, 2026 investor day, management set FY2027 revenue at US$12,000.0 million and FY2028 revenue at US$20,000.0 million. Those targets imply growth of 47.0% and 67.0%. Data center revenue is expected to reach US$18,000.0 million in FY2028, while the longer-range FY2031 target is US$70–90 billion. Because FY2031 is farther away, it also requires more execution that has not yet occurred.

The nearest test is the quarter ending October 2026. Marvell guided revenue of US$2,992.5–3,307.5 million. It also guided GAAP earnings per diluted share of US$0.48–0.58 and non-GAAP earnings of US$1.05–1.15. GAAP is the complete accounting result; non-GAAP removes selected costs such as share compensation and acquisition amortization. Neither measure alone equals cash available to spend.

blocks.heading: Has Marvell kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Marvell bought back US$2,040.1 million of shares in January 2026, yet diluted shares rose on an annual-average basis. The result is a reminder that buyback dollars do not automatically erase dilution. The company also said AI revenue substantially exceeded its US$1.5 billion target, but the June 2026 say-on-pay vote passed with 258.6 million votes against. Growth delivered does not settle whether shareholders paid too much for it.

blocks.heading: How have Marvell's revenue and profit changed?

paragraphs.text: Revenue reached $8,194.6 million in FY2026, up 42.1%, after only 4.7% growth in FY2025 and a 7.0% decline in FY2024. Across eight quarters, revenue rose from $1,516.1 million to $2,739.3 million. The steady quarterly climb confirms strong demand, but the uneven annual history shows a chip business that moves with customers’ construction plans.

Revenue reached $2,739.3 million, compared with $2,006.1 million a year earlier. Gross margin improved to 53.1% from 50.4%, and operating income rose to $459.7 million from $290.1 million. Marvell was selling more and retaining more operating profit from each sales dollar.
